Hi Mel, Kaz here (I'm a physio). I can't diagnose anything without seeing your leg, but what you describe is a really common overload pattern for the Achilles. Big jump in k's, stiff in the morning, sore a few cm above the heel, no pop. It usually responds well to sorting out the load.

First, a correction to the stretching advice above. Stretching hard until it burns tends to irritate this kind of pain rather than fix it, so I'd skip it. I'd also steer well clear of cortisone near the Achilles. It can weaken the tendon, and that's not a risk worth taking.

You don't need to stop completely, but don't push on as is either. Drop your weekly k's back, keep runs easy and flat, and leave out hills and speedwork for a bit.

A good guide is pain up to about 3/10 while you're running or loading it, as long as it's settled by the next morning. If it's worse the next day, or the morning stiffness is getting worse, you did too much, so back off a notch.

For strengthening, heel drops are fine, but heavy slow calf raises have better evidence these days. Go slow (about 3 seconds up, 3 down), a few sets of 8 to 12 every second day, and add weight once they feel easy. On the sore days, isometric holds are a good option. Rise up onto your toes and hold for 30 to 45 seconds, a few times over.

If it's not settling in 3 to 4 weeks, get it looked at by any sports physio near you in Bayswater. You'll get a proper assessment and a plan that fits your Rottnest build.

If you get a sudden pop, a feeling like you've been kicked in the back of the leg, or you can't push off, stop running and the calf work and get it checked the same day, at a GP or ED. That could be a rupture and shouldn't wait.

One more general thing: some antibiotics, particularly the fluoroquinolone family, are linked with tendon problems. If you've been on any lately, mention it to your doctor.

Good luck with the build for Feb!

reasons: It does not specifically address Mel’s post-run limping when advising whether to continue running.
